title: Greedy maximin start with radius growth
spec: Build random-restart starts like this. Sample 400 candidate points in the unit square. Pick n of them greedily so that each new point is the farthest from the already chosen ones and from the walls (maximin with a random first point). Set the initial radius of each point to 0.4 times its nearest-neighbour or wall distance. Use these as x0 for SLSQP in half of the restarts.

title: Hex-row starts with random row counts
spec: For half of fresh random starts, choose a random partition of 26 into 5 or 6 rows with counts between 3 and 6. Place rows at evenly spaced y values in [0.1,0.9], circles evenly spaced in x with a random half-offset on alternate rows, plus Gaussian jitter sd 0.02. Initial radius 0.06. Other half stay uniform random.

title: Perturbation share sweep: 15% random then local search
spec: Change the random-restart share from 0.3 to 0.15 in the solve loop condition (0.3 * TIME_FRACTION * time_limit becomes 0.15 * ...), so more time goes to perturbing the best packing, which was the only thing that helped.

title: Basin hopping from best with local perturbation
spec: Split time: first 40% of the budget runs random-restart SLSQP as now to find the best packing. Then loop until 80% of time: copy the best (c, r), pick 1-3 random circles (bias toward the smallest radii), relocate them to random positions with radius 0.02, add Gaussian jitter (sd 0.01) to all centres, run SLSQP (MAX_ITER 200) from this start, repair, and accept if the sum of radii improves. Keep the best throughout.

title: Restart share 15% then perturbation search
spec: In solve(), change the threshold for switching from fresh random restarts to perturbation of the best packing from 0.3*TIME_FRACTION*time_limit to 0.15*TIME_FRACTION*time_limit. Keep everything else from the current code unchanged. Slot 7 suggested a smaller restart share is better.

title: Window re-solve (large neighbourhood)
spec: In the perturbation phase, pick a random point in the square. Pick the 6-8 circles nearest to it. Re-initialise those circles to random centres inside their bounding box, with radius 0.03. Keep the other circles fixed at the best packing's values, and run SLSQP on all variables for 200 iterations. Accept the result if the repaired sum improves. Use this for half of the perturbations in place of the 2-3 circle move.

title: Combine two-stage SLSQP with perturbation search
spec: Keep the 30% restart / perturbation structure. In _solve_once, run SLSQP first with maxiter=40, then restart SLSQP from its result with maxiter=160 (and the same constraints). Use the two-stage for every call, both fresh and perturbed starts. Do not change anything else.

title: Hex-row starts with random row counts
spec: Initialise random-restart starts from rows of circles: pick a random number of rows from 4 to 6, split n circles among rows as evenly as possible with a random permutation of the extra counts, place each row at evenly spaced y and the circles at evenly spaced x with a random half-spacing offset on alternate rows. Add jitter of sd 0.02 and use radius 0.05. Use this for 50% of the restarts.

title: Bolder: large neighbourhood re-solve of a spatial window
spec: In the perturbation phase, a third of the moves pick a random point in the square and take the 5 to 7 circles nearest to it. Re-place those circles at random positions inside their joint bounding box, with radius 0.03, and keep the other circles fixed at their current centres and radii. Run a short SLSQP (60 iterations) over all variables, then 140 more. Accept the result if the repaired sum improves.

title: Warm start from a 25-circle optimum plus two inserts
spec: For some fresh starts, solve 24 circles with SLSQP (150 iterations) from a random start. Insert 2 new circles at the two largest holes (found by random point sampling) with radius 0.02, then run the full 26-circle SLSQP. Use this for 40% of the fresh starts in the restart phase and keep the incumbent perturbation phase.

title: Early abort of bad restarts via short SLSQP stage
spec: In the fresh restart phase, run SLSQP with maxiter=30 first and compute the sum of radii. Only continue with maxiter=170 more iterations from that point if the sum is at least the 60th percentile of the previous first-stage sums, or if fewer than 5 were recorded. Otherwise discard and move on. Track first-stage sums in a list inside solve().

title: Penalty-based warmup then SLSQP
spec: Before SLSQP, run 100 steps of a cheap vectorized gradient-style relaxation on the centres and radii. The objective is -sum(r) + mu * sum(max(0, overlap)^2) plus the wall violations, with mu growing from 1 to 1000 and step size 0.01. Use plain numpy with analytic gradients. Then hand this state to SLSQP with maxiter 150. Starting near feasibility should make each SLSQP run converge to better optima.

title: Maximin starts, restart share 20%
spec: Use the slot 34 maximin start for half of fresh starts and the original single-circle-move perturbation phase, but change the restart share from 0.3 to 0.2 of the budget. This tests whether a shorter random phase pays off when starts are better. Change only the share constant and the start generator.

title: Hex/grid structured starts with jitter
spec: Replace the uniform random init by structured starts. Pick a random row pattern for 26 circles, e.g. rows of counts like 5,5,5,5,6 or 6,5,6,5,4 (randomly choose from a few patterns summing to 26). Place centres evenly in each row, with rows evenly spaced in y and with alternate rows offset in x. Add jitter of sd 0.02 and set initial radii to 0.07. Use these in every restart, with the pattern and jitter drawn from rng.

title: Bounded variables with radius cap
spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.2]. Radius-ordered scaling is not needed. Combine this with a perturbation phase that jitters only the 8 circles with the smallest radii, with sd 0.04, and then polishes everything. Replicate the result because single runs are noisy.

title: Greedy radius-growth start
spec: Replace the fresh random start with a constructive one: sample 300 candidate points, and repeatedly add the point that has the largest possible radius, defined as min(wall distance, distance to the nearest placed circle minus that circle's radius), until 26 circles are placed. Use these centres and radii (floored at 0.01) as the SLSQP start. Do this for 50% of fresh starts, and add noise sd 0.01 to the centres.

title: Two-population restart with hybrid share tuning
spec: Set the restart share to 20% instead of 30% of the budget. In the perturbation phase, keep two incumbents. The first is the global best. The second is the best from a fresh random start made after the 20% mark. Alternate perturbation rounds between them. Every 25 rounds, replace the second incumbent with a new fresh-start result if the second one has not improved. Use shake sd 0.05, 60 SLSQP iterations, and accept only on improvement, as in the shake scheme.

title: Remove-and-reinsert at the largest hole
spec: New perturbation move for 1/3 of perturbations. Remove the 1-2 smallest-radius circles from the best packing. Estimate the largest empty hole with 2000 random points in the square, and keep the point that maximises the min over circles of (distance to centre minus radius) and the wall distance. Put the removed circles at that point, or at the second-best point if it is at least 0.1 away, with radius 0.02. Then run SLSQP on all circles and keep the result if it is better.

title: Remove-and-reinsert at the largest hole
spec: In the perturbation phase, for a third of perturbations: delete the smallest circle, then place it at the point of a 40x40 grid with the maximal distance to the surrounding circle edges and walls (max of min(dist to centres minus radii, wall distance)), with initial radius 0.5 times that clearance. Then run SLSQP as usual. Keep the existing perturbations for the other two thirds.

title: Early-abort restarts via short SLSQP stage
spec: In the restart phase, run each fresh start for 30 SLSQP iterations first and compute the repaired sum of radii. If it is below the 60th percentile of the first-stage sums seen so far (once at least 5 have been seen), discard it. Otherwise continue with 170 more iterations from that point. This spends more of the budget on promising basins. Keep the 30% restart / perturbation split.

title: Remove-and-reinsert at the largest hole
spec: New perturbation move, used with probability 1/4. Remove the circle with the smallest radius. Sample 2000 random points and take the one with the largest distance-to-nearest-circle-edge (min over j of d minus r_j, and wall distance). Put the circle there with radius equal to that clearance. Then run the normal SLSQP. Accept if the repaired sum improves.

title: Fixed-count local search from top-k pool
spec: Keep a pool of the 4 best distinct solutions. Each iteration, choose one at random, perturb it, re-optimize, and replace the worst in the pool if the result is better. This keeps diversity.

title: Greedy maximin-start with radius growth
spec: Build initial centres by farthest-point sampling. Draw 200 random candidate points in the unit square, then pick 26 one at a time, each maximising the minimum distance to the points already chosen and to the walls. Set each initial radius to 0.45 times the distance to its nearest neighbour or wall. Use this for 30% of the random restarts, with a small jitter of sd 0.01 so the starts differ.

title: Maximin starts plus staggered-row starts mixture
spec: For fresh random starts choose one of three init types with equal probability: uniform random, farthest-point maximin centres from 400 candidates, and jittered staggered rows (5 or 6 rows with random row counts summing to 26, jitter sd 0.02). Perturbation phase and the rest stay as in the incumbent.

title: Alternate LP radii and centre steps
spec: After each SLSQP in the perturbation phase, run 3 rounds of: (a) solve the LP for the radii with the centres fixed, using scipy linprog highs, maximising the sum of radii under pair and wall constraints; (b) a short SLSQP of 30 iterations on all variables from that point. Keep the best valid result. Apply this only to candidates whose first-stage sum is within 0.003 of the best.

title: Wider initial region with mixed radii
spec: Set INIT_LOW to 0.03 so initial centres are uniform in [0.03,0.97]. Draw initial radii from a log-uniform mixture, 0.02 to 0.14 per circle, sorted at random. Apply this to fresh starts only. Leave the perturbation phase untouched. Replicate the result at least twice, because of the noise sd of 0.0023.

title: Swap two circles of different radii
spec: Add a perturbation move: choose two circles with noticeably different radii (ratio > 1.3), swap their centres, set both radii to the smaller of the two times 0.8, and re-run SLSQP. Use it with probability 0.3 in the perturbation phase, in addition to the existing moves.

title: Window re-solve with shake-all alternation
spec: In the perturbation phase alternate three moves by random choice: (a) window re-solve (re-initialise the 6-8 circles nearest a random point at random positions with radius 0.03, then SLSQP all), (b) shake all centres with sd 0.05 then 60-iteration SLSQP followed by full SLSQP, (c) existing 2-3 circle relocation. Accept only if sum of repaired radii improves. Combines slots 45 and 31.

title: Maximin starts as base with 20% restart share
spec: Make half of fresh random starts use farthest-point maximin centres: for each start, pick the first centre uniformly in [0.05,0.95]^2 and then repeatedly add the candidate (out of 300 uniform random points per step) with the largest minimum distance to the chosen centres and to the walls. Initial radii 0.05. Set the restart share to 20% of the time budget (replace 0.3 in the perturbation switch) and keep the existing perturbation phase. This combines the replicated winners (slots 34 and 61) into one base.

title: Staggered-row starts plus window re-solve combined
spec: Combine two partly accepted ideas. Half of fresh random starts use jittered staggered rows: pick 5 rows, with counts from a random permutation of [5,5,6,5,5], x positions evenly spaced with a random offset, jitter sd 0.02, initial radius 0.05. In the perturbation phase (after 30% of the budget), half of the perturbations re-initialise the 6-8 circles nearest a random point at random positions inside that disc, with radius 0.03, then run SLSQP on all circles. Keep the best-so-far logic unchanged. Replicate the result.

title: Staggered-row starts plus maximin mix
spec: For fresh starts choose uniformly among three generators: uniform random centres, farthest-point maximin centres (200 candidates), and jittered staggered rows (5 or 6 rows with row counts summing to 26, alternate rows offset by half a spacing, jitter sd 0.02). Keep the existing perturbation phase at 25% restart share. Replicate-friendly combination of slots 41 and 34.

title: Population with crossover of halves
spec: Keep a pool of the 6 best distinct packings from the restart phase (distinct if sum of radii differs by more than 1e-4). In the second phase, with probability 0.4 create a child by taking circles with centre x<t from parent A and x>=t from parent B (t uniform in 0.35-0.65), fix the count to 26 by dropping the smallest extras or adding random circles of radius 0.03, then SLSQP and repair. Else perform the usual perturbation of the best. Insert children into the pool if they beat the worst.

title: Warm start from 25-circle solution plus 1 new circle
spec: In half of the restarts in the perturbation phase, take the best packing and remove the circle with the smallest radius. Re-insert it at the centre of the largest hole. Find the hole by evaluating 2000 random points and picking the one with the largest minimum of (distance to the nearest centre minus its radius) and the wall distance. Set its radius to 0.5 times that margin and run SLSQP.

title: Wider initial region mixed radii
spec: Draw initial centres uniform in [0.03, 0.97] instead of INIT_LOW 0.1. Draw initial radii from a log-uniform range of [0.02, 0.14], sorted so that larger radii are assigned to centres nearer the middle. Keep the rest unchanged.

title: Simulated-annealing acceptance in the perturbation phase
spec: Maintain the current packing and the best packing separately. Perturb the current one (move 1-3 circles or jitter) and re-solve. Accept the result if it is better, or with probability exp((new-cur)/T). T decays geometrically from 0.004 to 0.0003 over the phase. Return the best seen. This lets the search leave local optima instead of always restarting from the best.

title: Maximin starts plus shake-all perturbation
spec: Half of fresh random starts use farthest-point sampling: draw 400 uniform candidates in [0.03,0.97]^2, pick the first at random, then repeatedly add the candidate with the largest min distance to those already chosen until n are picked. Use initial radius 0.05. In the perturbation phase, every perturbation shakes all centres with Gaussian sd 0.05, clips to [0.01,0.99], and runs SLSQP with MAX_ITER=60 from the shaken state, with radii set to 0.8 times the current radii. Accept only if the repaired sum is better than the best.

title: Radius-growth penalty continuation
spec: For fresh starts, solve a sequence of SLSQP problems that maximize sum(r) with radii upper bounds cap = 0.06, 0.09, 0.13 (via bounds), 40 iterations each, warm-started from the previous result, then a final 100 iterations with no cap. The cap prevents early large circles from locking in a bad topology. Use for half of fresh starts.
